groups.name: BIM authoring
groups.sub: Plans, sections, elevations and schedules drawn from one building model.

groups.name: 2D and 3D drafting
groups.sub: Plans and details drawn in DWG, shared as files and external references.

groups.name: 3D modeling
groups.sub: Massing, form and design studies by editing geometry directly.

groups.name: In the browser
groups.sub: Newer tools that run in a web browser, several people in one file.

groups.name: Free and open source
groups.sub: No license fee for professional work. Check each one's file exchange before a project depends on it.

tools.name: Revit
notes: RVT is the standard working format for US architectural, structural and MEP coordination. Worksharing puts several people in one model on a local server. Cloud worksharing needs a separate entitlement.
Windows only. On a Mac it runs through Windows in a virtual machine or on a separate PC.
tools.meta: Price: $3,012 a year or $380 a month. AEC Collection $3,675 a year or $460 a month. Flex: $99 for 33 tokens, and Revit uses 10 tokens a day · Website

tools.name: Archicad
notes: BIM on Windows and Mac, with Teamwork and BIMcloud for several people in one model.
Revit exchange carries 3D geometry in and out, not an editable Revit project. Agree on IFC or DWG with consultants who work in Revit.
tools.meta: Price: Studio from $2,414 a year, Collaborate from $2,840 a year · Website

tools.name: Vectorworks Architect
notes: 2D drafting, 3D modeling and BIM in one app on Windows and Mac, also used for landscape and stage work. Project Sharing puts several people in one file.
It imports Revit projects and families. It does not save RVT.
tools.meta: Price: Architect $1,530 a year or $170 a month. Design Suite, with landscape tools and library, $1,980 a year or $220 a month · Website

tools.name: Allplan
notes: Architecture and structure in one model, with reinforcement and precast detailing. Common in Germany and central Europe.
RVT import has version limits. Check the data exchange list for the Revit version your consultants use.
tools.meta: Price: Pro $3,588 a year · Website

tools.name: Chief Architect Premier
notes: Residential design from house plans to framing, roofs, cabinets, 3D views and permit sets. Home Designer is the consumer version.
tools.meta: Price: $1,995 a year · Website

tools.name: BricsCAD BIM
notes: BIM on native DWG with AutoCAD-style commands, built on BricsCAD Pro. The only BIM authoring app here that runs on Linux.
Revit files come in as geometry. Shared work is file-based, as in DWG drafting.
tools.meta: Price: $1,166 a year or $2,616 perpetual · Website

tools.name: AutoCAD
notes: Drafting in DWG. Plans, sections and schedules are coordinated by hand, and shared work runs through files and external references.
The Mac version lacks some Windows features and add-ons. The web and mobile apps view and edit drawings with a reduced command set.
tools.meta: Price: $2,095 a year. AEC Collection $3,675 a year or $460 a month. Flex: AutoCAD uses 7 tokens a day. AutoCAD LT, 2D only, costs less · Website

tools.name: BricsCAD Lite / Pro
notes: DWG drafting with AutoCAD-style commands on Windows, Mac and Linux. Lite is 2D. Pro adds 3D modeling, point clouds and third-party apps.
IFC and Revit import are in BricsCAD BIM, not Lite or Pro.
tools.meta: Price: Lite $345 a year or $780 perpetual. Pro $780 a year or $1,752 perpetual · Website

tools.name: ZWCAD
notes: Standard covers 2D drafting, annotation and plotting in DWG. Professional adds 3D modeling, IFC editing and RVT import.
Perpetual licenses, Windows only.
tools.meta: Price: Standard $899, Professional $1,399 perpetual · Website

tools.name: SketchUp Pro
notes: Surface modeling on Windows, Mac, iPad and the web, with a large library of models and extensions. LayOut turns model views into scaled, dimensioned sheets.
The Revit Importer runs on Windows and is in eligible plans. Files are shared through Trimble Connect, one person editing at a time.
tools.meta: Price: Pro $399 a year. Go and Studio plans are also offered · Website

tools.name: Rhino + Grasshopper
notes: NURBS modeling for freeform surfaces, with Grasshopper built in for geometry defined by parameters and a graph of operations. VisualARQ, a paid plug-in, adds BIM objects and IFC on Windows.
Rhino.Inside.Revit runs Rhino and Grasshopper inside Revit on Windows. Shared work is file-based, through worksessions of linked files.
tools.meta: Price: $995 one-time, upgrade $595. A 90-day evaluation is free · Website

tools.name: Motif Design
notes: Browser BIM authoring and drawing sets, with AI agents that work in the same model as the team. Access is arranged through Motif after a demo request.

Revit and Rhino models stream in, and IFC files import. Motif does not say whether it reads DWG, so a DWG can go in through Rhino or Revit first. Nothing exports back to Revit yet. Motif Review, for reviewing models and sheets, is a separate product.
tools.meta: Price: Design $150 a month, Review $25 a month · Website

tools.name: Qonic
notes: Opens large RVT and IFC models in the browser for coordination, quantities and editing. A Revit plugin moves changes both ways.
Since April 2026 it draws annotated plans and sections from the model that update with it, exported to DWG.
tools.meta: Price: depends on configuration. The full configuration is $240 a month or $2,582 a year · Website

tools.name: Forma
notes: Site analysis and schematic design in the browser. Building Design, added in April 2026, is included with Revit and the AEC Collection.
Autodesk says Forma will replace Revit over time, with no date. It does not draw construction documents.
tools.meta: Price: $700 a year. Flex: 6 tokens a day · Website

tools.name: Snaptrude
notes: Concept to schematic design in the browser. Models start from a brief or a sketch, drawings update live, and several people work in a model at once.
Snaptrude describes Revit exchange as two-way, but its own pages and release notes disagree on how. Test a round trip with your Revit version first.
tools.meta: Price: Solo $60 a month, Organization $100 a month · Website

tools.name: Arcol
notes: Early-stage design: massing, floor plans, area metrics and presentation boards in one shared browser file.

DWG and DXF import as references to trace and snap to, and IFC imports with other 3D formats. Exports are GLB, STL, CSV and, on paid plans, massing to Revit through an add-in. It is not a construction documents tool.
tools.meta: Price: $100 a month · Website

tools.name: Rayon
notes: Shared 2D plans in the browser, used for interiors and space planning. Imports DWG, DXF and PDF, and several people edit one file at once.
Rayon says its fourth version, due by the end of 2026, adds 3D.
tools.meta: Price: $21 a month, with DWG $38 a month · Website

tools.name: FreeCAD
notes: A parametric 3D modeler with the BIM workbench built in since version 1.0: walls, slabs, windows, stairs, structure, spaces, schedules and section planes. It can work on IFC files directly, so objects are read and written as IFC. Plans, sections and elevations are views of the model placed on TechDraw pages at the page’s scale.

It has no DWG code of its own. It converts DWG to DXF and back through an external converter, such as LibreDWG or the free ODA File Converter. There is no RVT import, so exchange with Revit goes through IFC. Files are for one person at a time.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (LGPL) · Website

tools.name: Bonsai
notes: An add-on for Blender, installed from Blender’s Get Extensions tab. Every object, property and relationship is stored as IFC, so the IFC file is the project file, not an export. It covers spatial structure, classifications, schedules and quantities, with costing, 4D scheduling and COBie tools.

Drawings are generated from the model as SVG and annotated. Bonsai’s own documentation calls the drafting tools early-stage, and the plan and section guides are marked work in progress. Git tracks revisions of the IFC file. Merging other people’s changes needs the separate ifcmerge tool and is experimental. It does not read DWG or RVT.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source · Bonsai Viewer, a standalone IFC viewer, is separate · Website

tools.name: Blender
notes: A general 3D modeler of meshes and curves that architects use for massing, form studies and detailed models, with its own renderer. It has no building objects, dimensions or sheet layouts. BIM elements, IFC and drawings come from the Bonsai add-on.
DXF import is a community extension offered as-is. Blender does not read DWG or RVT. Current Mac builds need Apple silicon.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL) · Website

tools.name: LibreCAD
notes: 2D drafting with layers, blocks, dimensions and hatches, printing to PDF and SVG. It has no 3D.
DXF is its native format. It reads DWG. Saving DWG needs a build compiled with DWG support, so check the download before you plan to send DWG to a consultant.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPLv2) · Website

tools.name: QCAD Community Edition
notes: 2D drafting with layers, blocks, dimensions, hatching and a large part library. The Community Edition is open source and saves DXF.

DWG reading and writing comes with QCAD Professional, a paid add-on. The download is the Professional trial, which runs in time-limited sessions. Removing the trial add-on leaves the free Community Edition.
tools.meta: Price: Community Edition free, open source. Professional is a paid license · Website

tools.name: SketchUp Free
notes: SketchUp’s modeler in the browser, with 10 GB of Trimble Connect storage. It does not include LayOut, so there are no drawing sheets. It imports SKP, JPG and PNG. DWG and other CAD formats need a paid plan.
Trimble’s terms limit free versions to non-commercial use outside production, so it is not for paid project work.
tools.meta: Price: Free for non-commercial use · Terms · Website

tools.name: Sweet Home 3D
notes: Home and interior layout. Draw walls, rooms, doors and windows in plan, place furniture from a library, and see the 3D view update. The plan prints and exports to PDF and vector images, and the model exports to OBJ.
It is for houses and interiors, not construction documents. The desktop and browser versions are free and open source. The iPad, iPhone and Android app is paid.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL). Mobile app paid · Website

tools.name: OpenArch BIM
notes: A BIM application written from scratch in Rust for Windows, Mac and Linux. It models layered walls, floors, roofs and families, and draws plans, elevations, sections and schedules from them.

Its README says it is in early development and not ready for project work. Sheets, title blocks and PDF, DXF and IFC export are planned. There are no published releases yet, so running it means building it from source.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (AGPL-3.0) · Website

tools.name: BIMopen
notes: A BIM modeler that runs in the browser, with test builds for Windows, Linux and Android. Plans export as SVG, sheets as PDF, and schedules and quantities as CSV. It exports IFC4 and opens IFC2x3 and IFC4 files. The site is in Italian.
Its maker says it already models simple buildings. Suspended ceilings, phases, loadable families and DWG export are still missing. The source is not public yet.
tools.meta: Price: Free · Website

tools.name: CadCraft
notes: 2D drafting and documentation by command line, with layers, blocks, dimensions and plottable layouts, meant to feel familiar to AutoCAD users. One of eight free apps from the same maker, covering drafting, BIM, modeling, markup, takeoff, civil, detailing and parts.

The apps ship together in CadCraft Studio for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android, and early builds run in the browser. The downloads are not code-signed yet, so the operating system warns the first time they open. Saving in the browser waits for a paid team plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache-2.0). SuperCad Studio, which is to combine the eight apps in one window, is a separate commercial product at $250 a seat · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: BimCraft
notes: BIM authoring: parametric walls, doors and windows on levels and grids, with views, schedules, sheets and clash checks. Its maker says it will feel familiar to Revit users. It does not open or save RVT, so exchange with Revit goes through IFC.

The apps ship together in CadCraft Studio for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android, and early builds run in the browser. The downloads are not code-signed yet, so the operating system warns the first time they open. Saving in the browser waits for a paid team plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache-2.0). SuperCad Studio, which is to combine the eight apps in one window, is a separate commercial product at $250 a seat · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: ModelCraft
notes: Push-pull 3D modeling for massing and early design, with groups, components, guides and inference snapping.

The apps ship together in CadCraft Studio for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android, and early builds run in the browser. The downloads are not code-signed yet, so the operating system warns the first time they open. Saving in the browser waits for a paid team plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache-2.0). SuperCad Studio, which is to combine the eight apps in one window, is a separate commercial product at $250 a seat · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: LumberCAD
notes: Planning for builds in dimensional lumber, for people without CAD experience. Drag and snap from a catalog of more than 100 components rather than modeling them. It keeps a live cut list that splits parts into stock lengths, and builds PDF documents with views, elevations, foundations and material lists.

It exports STEP, OBJ, STL, DXF and GLB, and saves its own .lcad format, which no other app opens. A shared link lets others view and copy a build, not edit it. Its makers say it does not do the structural or engineering analysis of general CAD tools.
tools.meta: Price: Free during the public beta. The price after the beta is undecided · Website

tools.name: IngeTrazo
notes: A 3D modeler for architecture and engineering, made in Peru. Draw lines and shapes, push a face into a solid, and type exact lengths from the keyboard. An optional BIM layer tags what you drew as walls, slabs, columns or doors, lists their quantities as CSV, and exports IFC 4. Its makers say that layer is still in development.

Sheets hold views at exact scale, with dimensions tied to the model, hidden-line and section styles, and a title block, and print to vector PDF. It imports DWG, DXF, SketchUp .skp files of every version, OBJ, COLLADA, glTF, STL and IFC, and exports DXF, COLLADA, glTF and OBJ. DWG import does not work on Mac yet. It also places a project on real terrain with satellite imagery and survey points in UTM.

An AI assistant inside the app works with your own key for Groq, Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, DeepSeek or a local model, and an MCP bridge lets Claude Desktop and Claude Code draw in the open app. The same author makes IngeCAD, a 2D drafting app for Linux, and IngePresupuestos, for cost estimating from IFC.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (GPL-3.0), with no paid editions · Website · Source
